one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban reveals an unknown bond between the recently deceased Washington SyCip (who passed at 96) and Cardinal Chito Tagle: SyCip would whisper to the author that Tagle was 'the most brilliant Catholic I have ever met -- an intellectual giant, but beyond that, humble, prayerful and compassionate' -- and express his wish to become Catholic so he could greet Tagle in the Vatican. Tagle, texting from Spain upon hearing of SyCip's death, called him 'my quiet and hidden friend' -- a mystery and a blessing. The author describes meeting SyCip only after retiring from the SC in December 2006, becoming fellow independent directors and advisers of PLDT, MPIC, First Philippine Holdings, Jollibee, Asian Terminals, and Metrobank, and fellow trustees of FLP, Tan Yan Kee, and Metrobank foundations. He encapsulates SyCip's legacy as the 'ICE of Wash' -- Integrity (not just honesty but intellectual decency, moral courage, active fairness, and the expectation that scholars give back more than they received), Competence (no shortcuts, no mid-merits, no compromise with mediocrity -- 'Hindi puede ang puede na'), and Education (Synergeia Foundation for basic schooling; AIM co-founded with Ayala and Lopez for graduate work; education as the poor's passage to prosperity). SyCip brought the same passion to FLP's three legal-education projects -- 15 professorial chairs in 15 law schools, 21 full law scholarships, and a legal dissertation contest -- as to AIM and Synergeia, despite their relatively minor scale.
